docs.text: Thunderbird Add-on (Verifier) ¶ Purpose Verify provenance headers in Thunderbird using the Nicrypt-Stego API. What it verifies - Message provenance via X-Provenance-* headers. - Attachment provenance via X-Provenance-Attachment . - A single badge verdict via POST /v1/provenance/verdict (recommended). Prerequisites - API running at http://127.0.0.1:8125/v1 - A valid JWT token (see docs/quickstart.md ) - A message that passed through the gateway relay/inbound flow Install (temporary add-on) 1) Open Thunderbird. 2) Tools -> Add-ons and Themes -> gear icon -> Debug Add-ons. 3) Load Temporary Add-on and select: poc/thunderbird-addon/manifest.json Install (packaged) 1) Build the add-on: make package-addons 2) Install the generated XPI: dist/addons/thunderbird-addon.xpi Configure settings 1) Click the add-on toolbar button or open Add-ons and choose Options. 2) Set: - API Base: http://127.0.0.1:8125/v1 - API Token: your JWT 3) Click Save Settings. Verify a message - Select a message, then: - Click the toolbar button and press "Verify Selected", or - Right-click a message -> Verify provenance, or - Use shortcut: Ctrl+Shift+V Stego (invisible text) test 1) Generate and send a stego email: python scripts/send_stego_email.py \ --token $TOKEN \ --secret "alice@example.com|2026-02-17|Stego QA" \ --cover "a short compliance memo about retention policies" \ --from "sender@example.com" \ --to "your-thunderbird-inbox@example.com" 2) Open the email in Thunderbird and run "Verify Selected". Plain email + provenance headers (gateway relay) Use this when you want a normal human message and header-only provenance: python scripts/send_plain_gateway_email.py \ --token $TOKEN \ --secret "alerts@yourbank.com|2026-02-17|Bank Notice" \ --from "alerts@yourbank.com" \ --to "your-thunderbird-inbox@example.com" \ --subject "Account notice" \ --body "Hello, this is your bank. Please review the update." Expected results - Verified: shows sender/provenance string, model hash, timestamp, policy. - Partial: message verified but some attachments fail. - Unverified: missing headers or policy failure. Gateway flow required (recommended) Messages must pass through the gateway to include the provenance headers. One-command gateway bootstrap: make bootstrap-gateway ENABLE_IMAP=0 Provenance secret Set PROVENANCE_SECRET to control what appears as "Sender" in verification results. Example: PROVENANCE_SECRET="sender@example.com|2026-02-17|Email QA" Notes - Thunderbird can read full headers; no Gmail-style body stamping is required. - If you see "Policy: missing_provenance", the message did not pass through the gateway.

docs.text: University Pitch: Nicrypt-Stego ¶ One-liner Provenance you can prove: embed cryptographic authorship and policy metadata inside academic text so universities can verify origin, compliance, and integrity. Problem Universities increasingly rely on AI-assisted writing, but cannot reliably prove authorship, compliance, or provenance once text leaves the system. This creates risk for research integrity, grant audits, and institutional reputation. Solution Nicrypt-Stego embeds encrypted provenance directly into text. Outputs look normal, can be published anywhere, and remain verifiable by the institution using internal keys. Why it matters for universities - Research integrity: prove that outputs came from approved workflows. - Grant compliance: embed grant ID, PI, and policy version into reports. - Academic integrity: detect tampering or unverified AI use. - Publishing: certify authorship for internal journals and preprints. How it works 1) Encrypt provenance metadata (PI, grant, department, date). 2) Embed into text using steganographic token selection. 3) Verify later with cryptographic proof and model hash. Deployment fit (on-prem) - Works fully on-prem for privacy. - Supports internal LLMs and private data. - Integrates with existing email, CMS, and research pipelines. Pilot plan (4–6 weeks) 1) Select one department or lab. 2) Embed provenance into a real workflow (grant report or internal memo). 3) Verify against archive/audit pipeline. 4) Expand to campus-wide policy adoption. Pricing model - Campus-wide annual license (tiered by enrollment). - Departmental licenses for decentralized budgets. - Optional support/SLA and compliance reporting add-ons. Call to action Launch a low-risk pilot with one department to validate integrity, compliance, and workflow fit.

docs.text: Upload Gateway (Provenance Proxy) ¶ Goal - Sit between uploaders and existing document portals. - Embed provenance automatically while keeping documents readable. - Forward the same files to the institution’s existing storage/archive. High-Level Flow 1) User uploads to gateway. 2) Gateway extracts text and encrypts provenance. 3) Gateway writes metadata into file (PDF/DOCX). 4) Gateway forwards file to the upstream portal (S3/SharePoint/ResearchGate/etc). 5) Gateway logs the audit record and returns receipt to user. Why this works - No change to archive/back-end systems. - Minimal workflow change for users. - Provenance embedded before storage, preserved at rest. Core Components - Upload API (multipart form): /v1/gateway/upload - Metadata embedder (PDF/DOCX) - Upstream connector (S3, SharePoint, ResearchGate, custom API) - Audit log + receipt ID - Optional verification endpoint for downstream checks Gateway API (proposed) POST /v1/gateway/upload Headers - Authorization: Bearer Response headers (gateway) - X-Provenance-Ciphertext - X-Provenance-Model - X-Provenance-BPT - X-Provenance-Timestamp - X-Provenance-Attachment (per file) Body (multipart/form-data) - file: binary - secret: string - metadata_mode: "pdf" | "docx" | "auto" - upstream_target: "s3" | "sharepoint" | "custom" - upstream_url: string (optional for custom) Example (local embed + forward) curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8125/v1/gateway/upload \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ -F "file=@paper.pdf" \ -F "secret=alice@example.com|2026-02-15|Paper" \ -F "author=Alice Johnson" \ -F "title=Provenance Research" \ -F "subject=Data Provenance" \ -F "keywords=provenance,compliance,ai" \ -F "metadata_mode=auto" \ -F "upstream_url=https://your-portal.example.com/upload" Presigned S3 upload curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8125/v1/gateway/upload \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ -F "file=@paper.pdf" \ -F "secret=alice@example.com|2026-02-15|Paper" \ -F "upstream_s3_bucket=my-bucket" \ -F "upstream_s3_key=archive/paper.pdf" \ -F "upstream_s3_presign=true" SharePoint connector (PUT) curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8125/v1/gateway/upload \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ -F "file=@paper.pdf" \ -F "secret=alice@example.com|2026-02-15|Paper" \ -F "upstream_sharepoint_url=https://tenant.sharepoint.com/sites/site/_api/web/GetFolderByServerRelativeUrl('Shared%20Documents')/Files/add(url='paper.pdf',overwrite=true)" \ -F "upstream_sharepoint_token=$SP_TOKEN" Extract metadata (verify later) curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8125/v1/gateway/metadata \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ -F "file=@paper.pdf" \ -F "provenance_only=true" \ -F 'expected_keys_json=["X-Provenance-Ciphertext","X-Provenance-Model","X-Provenance-Bpt","X-Provenance-Timestamp"]' Verify metadata (badge result) curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8125/v1/gateway/verify \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ -F "file=@paper.pdf" Batch upload curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8125/v1/gateway/upload_batch \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ -F "files=@paper.pdf" \ -F "manifest_json=$(cat manifest.json)" \ -F "strict_filename=false" Manifest example (supports local_path) { "items": [ { "filename": "paper.pdf", "local_path": "paper.pdf", "secret": "alice@example.com|2026-02-15|Paper", "metadata_mode": "auto" } ] } Response { "request_id": "req_abc123", "status": "forwarded", "ciphertext": "gAAAAAB...", "model_hash": "mhash_123456", "receipt_id": "rcpt_7890", "upstream_ref": "portal-asset-id" } Metadata embedding rules - PDF: XMP or custom metadata keys - X-Provenance-Ciphertext - X-Provenance-Model - X-Provenance-Bpt - X-Provenance-Timestamp - DOCX: custom document properties with same keys Upstream forwarding modes 1) Direct API proxy (HTTP/S3/SharePoint) 2) File drop (shared folder) 3) Email relay (for journals / repositories) Security & Compliance - Tenant-scoped keys and quotas. - Full audit log (append-only). - Optional request signing for upstream portals. Rollout Plan 1) Pilot on one repository (e.g., departmental archive). 2) Enable audit log + verification tooling. 3) Expand to multi-tenant orgs and portals.

docs.text: Windows Service Runbook ¶ Overview This runbook describes how to run the inbound and outbound SMTP daemons as Windows Services. Option A: NSSM (Recommended) 1) Download NSSM from https://nssm.cc/download 2) Install the inbound service: nssm install NicryptInbound "C:\Path\To\python.exe" "C:\Path\To\repo\poc\smtp_inbound_daemon.py" --listen-port 2527 nssm set NicryptInbound AppDirectory "C:\Path\To\repo" nssm set NicryptInbound AppEnvironmentExtra API_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:8125/v1 API_TOKEN=REPLACE_WITH_TOKEN STAMP_BODY=1 nssm start NicryptInbound 3) Install the outbound service: nssm install NicryptOutbound "C:\Path\To\python.exe" "C:\Path\To\repo\poc\smtp_relay.py" --listen-port 2525 nssm set NicryptOutbound AppDirectory "C:\Path\To\repo" nssm set NicryptOutbound AppEnvironmentExtra API_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:8125/v1 API_TOKEN=REPLACE_WITH_TOKEN nssm start NicryptOutbound PowerShell Helper Use poc/windows_setup.ps1 for a scripted install. Optional: add NSSM to PATH via -NssmPath . Makefile Bootstrap (checks NSSM) $Env:PYTHON_EXE="C:\Path\To\python.exe" $Env:API_BASE="http://127.0.0.1:8125/v1" $Env:API_TOKEN="REPLACE_WITH_TOKEN" $Env:NSSM_PATH="C:\Tools\nssm" make bootstrap-services Auto-download NSSM (Makefile) - make bootstrap-services will auto-download NSSM 2.24 to %TEMP% if not found in PATH. Option B: Task Scheduler (Minimal) Use Task Scheduler to run the daemons on startup with proper environment variables. Rollback nssm stop NicryptInbound nssm remove NicryptInbound confirm nssm stop NicryptOutbound nssm remove NicryptOutbound confirm

Quickstart ¶ This is the daily workflow cheat-sheet for running and verifying Nicrypt-Stego. 0) Start the API ¶ . .venv/bin/activate PYTHONPATH=apps/api JWT_SECRET=dev-secret uvicorn server.app:app --reload --port 8125 1) Create a full-scope JWT (dev) ¶ export TOKEN="$(JWT_SECRET=dev-secret python scripts/gen_token.py)" 1b) Issue a vendor license token (Sprint 9) ¶ If LICENSE_REQUIRED_FOR_EMBED=1 or LICENSE_REQUIRED_FOR_SIGNATURE=1 is enabled on the API, you must supply a license_token when issuing certificates or signature tokens. Issue a license (requires a JWT with licenses:issue ): curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8125/v1/licenses/issue \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "org_id":"public", "lic_id":"lic_demo", "ttl_seconds":3600, "features":{ "offline_embed":true, "signature_issue":true } }' Then export the returned value as LICENSE_TOKEN for later calls: export LICENSE_TOKEN="v1.<vendor_payload>.<vendor_sig>" 2) Embed provenance (text) ¶ curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8125/v1/provenance/embed \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "secret":"you@example.com|2026-02-15|Email QA", "cover_prompt":"a short compliance memo", "backend":"mvp", "bits_per_token":3, "max_new_tokens":700, "auto_expand":true, "auto_expand_margin":50 }' 2b) Standalone SDK smoke test (no API) ¶ If you see ValueError: Payload too large for max_new_tokens , estimate capacity first and set max_new_tokens = needed + margin . . .venv/bin/activate python - <<'PY' from nicrypt_stego.provenance import estimate_capacity, protect, verify secret = "alice@example.com|2026-02-15|SDK smoke" topic = "Subject: Test

Hello team,
This is a cover memo.
" cfg = dict( backend="mvp", model_name="sshleifer/tiny-gpt2", bits_per_token=3, # must match on verify() redundancy=1, ecc_mode="repetition", ecc_symbols=16, ) needed = estimate_capacity(secret, **cfg) max_new_tokens = needed + 50 stego = protect(secret=secret, topic=topic, max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens, **cfg) out = verify(stego_text=stego, topic=topic, max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens, **cfg) print("verified:", out == secret) print("extracted:", out) PY 3) Verify (ciphertext-only, recommended) ¶ curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8125/v1/provenance/verify \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "ciphertext":"gAAAAAB...", "model_name":"sshleifer/tiny-gpt2", "bits_per_token":4 }' 4) File embed ¶ curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8125/v1/provenance/embed_file \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ -F "file=@/path/doc.pdf" \ -F "cover_prompt=Policy update memo." \ -F "backend=mvp" \ -F "bits_per_token=3" \ -F "max_new_tokens=700" \ -F "auto_expand=true" \ -F "auto_expand_margin=50" 5) Verify email headers (recommended production) ¶ curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8125/v1/provenance/verify_headers \ -H
